scripts.//spike-filter: The '!@spike/*' filter EXCLUDES the @spike/* DEV-ONLY fixtures under examples/ (dev-server, the synthetic stream/agent packs) from CI build/test/typecheck. The @rayspec/local-boot spec-driven boot wrapper is a @rayspec/* member and IS covered by CI.
scripts.//test: `--concurrency=1` serializes turbo's package-level test tasks (one package's vitest at a time). WHY: `@rayspec/durable-dbos` + `@rayspec/server` are the only two packages that boot a REAL DBOS engine (DBOS.launch) and, run concurrently against the one shared local Postgres, cause catalog/pool pressure (deadlocks, CREATE/DROP-DATABASE lock races); separately, `@rayspec/cli`'s gen-handler typecheck test writes throwaway files into packages/kernel/platform/src and a concurrent `tsc -b` of platform/api-auth globs them mid-delete (TS6053). Serializing the turbo task graph removes both cross-package races. NOT MASKING A PROD BUG: this is a TEST-HARNESS artifact of N throwaway DBs + two engine-booting packages sharing ONE local Postgres; prod uses ONE app DB + ONE sys DB. Intra-package parallelism is unchanged (each vitest config still controls its own files); isolated `pnpm --filter X test` runs are unaffected (no `--concurrency` there). build/typecheck untouched. (Companion fix: `packages/app/cli/vitest.config.ts` raises the cli testTimeout to 60s so `cli/index.test.ts`'s in-process `plan` cold-start cannot trip the 5000ms default under full-suite CPU load. No wall-clock grace dependency remains: every suite that exercises the refresh grace window drives the injected clock the service also stamps `rotatedAt` from — `auth.test.ts`'s reuse-detection tests always did, and `org-selection-persistence.test.ts`'s ROTATED-cookie switch test now does too, so its rotate→switch hop no longer races the 30ms budget under load.)
scripts.//gate:api-report: A package promises a public surface by naming its report file in its own package.json ("rayspecPublicApi": "<path>"); this gate re-derives that report from the package's BUILT type declarations and byte-compares it to the committed one, so a change to the surface lands as a reviewable diff instead of an accident. Regenerate with `node scripts/check-public-api-report.mjs --write`. Runs AFTER `pnpm build` (it reads dist). A package that does not declare the marker is not scanned — the scanned set is DECLARED DATA, so zero declared packages is a legitimate PASS; everything about a package that HAS declared it (missing report, stale report, missing declarations, an export the parser cannot read, an exported name whose declaration is inside the package but out of the reader's reach) is fail-closed, and a report file no manifest claims fails too, so dropping the key cannot retire the guard while the artifact rots.
scripts.//gate:pack-migrations: An extension pack that brings its OWN migration chain declares the table prefix its objects live under; this scans every declared chain and fails on any CREATE TABLE / CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX whose name does not carry that prefix, on any ALTER TABLE or CREATE INDEX ... ON whose target does not, and on any statement outside the accepted additive set. The destructive half is not a second vocabulary written here: it runs the PLATFORM's own scan (`scanMigrationSql` from @rayspec/db) with an EMPTY allowlist, so 'a closed pack does not get a lower bar than the core' is a property of the wiring rather than a claim — the platform chain's reviewed allowlist has no counterpart here and no mechanism to author one. A declared chain that reads zero files is a FAILURE, not a skip, and so is an EMPTY declared set: emptying DECLARED_CHAINS cannot retire the guard while the committed chain rots. Runs AFTER `pnpm build` (it imports the scan from dist); needs no database.
scripts.gate: pnpm gate:chokepoint && pnpm gate:adapter-handlers && pnpm gate:handler-imports && pnpm gate:extension-capability && pnpm gate:spec-schema && pnpm gate:no-pack && pnpm gate:fixture-neutrality && pnpm gate:byte-identity && pnpm gate:sbom-fresh && pnpm gate:migrations && pnpm gate:pack-migrations && pnpm gate:shadow-dryrun && pnpm gate:migrate-clean && pnpm gate:parity && pnpm gate:no-archaeology && pnpm gate:skill-drift && pnpm gate:api-report
scripts.//release: scripts/publish.mjs is the ONLY sanctioned path to npm: it transiently stamps the release version (DERIVED from this manifest's `version`; --version only asserts it) + flips private:false + ensures files:['dist'] for the CLI runtime closure, then ALWAYS restores the committed tree (private:true stays the accidental-publish guard). `release:pack` and `release:dry-run` are no-write proofs; a real registry write is `node scripts/publish.mjs --publish --yes-really-publish` with RAYSPEC_ALLOW_PUBLISH=1 (founder release window). Requires `pnpm build` first.
scripts.//release-identity: scripts/release-identity.mjs emits the RELEASE IDENTITY MANIFEST — the artifact that maps the published closure back to the commit it was built from (version, source commit + worktree state, per-package tarball integrity and unpacked file-list digest, the three schema artifacts, the lockfile and dependency-SBOM digests, the Node/pnpm requirements, the tag and the build workflow run). It is UNSIGNED: there is no release workflow (see the scripts/publish.mjs docblock), so keyless CI signing would mean moving the release into CI; the manifest's authenticity comes from the authenticated release it is attached to. A release run is: (1) `pnpm build` and `rm -f packages/app/rayspec/rayspec-release-identity.json` — the manifest is gitignored and listed in the launcher's `files`, so a manifest left by the PREVIOUS release run would be packed into this release's launcher tarball, which no manifest generated for this release can match (packing is not byte-reproducible); step 3 refuses in that case rather than emitting an unverifiable manifest; (2) `node scripts/publish.mjs --pack --out release/v<version>`; (3) `pnpm release:identity --tarballs release/v<version>` — writes packages/app/rayspec/rayspec-release-identity.json, which the publish in step 5 packs into the launcher tarball it uploads; (4) `pnpm release:identity-verify --tarballs release/v<version>` — must print 0 failures; (5) publish per the //release note; (6) attach the manifest AND the tarballs it pins to the GitHub release: `gh release upload v<version> packages/app/rayspec/rayspec-release-identity.json release/v<version>/*.tgz`. Step 6 is the release-asset half of the manifest's reachability; the launcher tarball is the installed-package half.
